title: Homer and the Iliad and Odyssey
summary: Homer and the Iliad and Odyssey
description: Record first created by the Generations curriculum import (Preparing the World for Jesus (1st ed., 2020)). CFAH dates it as well (added by the CFAH pass); the sort follows the four-tier rule.

sorting_basis.note: Tier 2: CFAH Reply to Beckman (Griffith & White, Part 3): 914 - 866 BC. Sort changed by the Reply to Beckman pass (2026-11-13): was provisional 800 BC.

chronologies.citation: Griffith & White, "A Reply to Beckman’s Defense of Thiele’s Chronology, Part 3: The Founding Dates of Tyre and Carthage," OSF preprint v1.2 (2025), doi:10.17605/OSF.IO/9V65S, Table 2, row 914–866, p. 46
chronologies.note: Appearance of Homer; he may have flourished for up to 50 years, into the time of Lycurgus.

chronologies.citation: Preparing the World for Jesus (1st ed., 2020), ch. 13 "The Misguided Greeks and Alexander's Ill-Fated Empire (800–150 BC)", PDF p. 397 (printed p. 396)
chronologies.note: The siege of Troy is placed some 380 years earlier.
chronologies.edition_note: 1st ed. (2020); superseded by the 2nd ed. (2024), which prints "around 800 BC" (PDF p. 567): the same date.

chronologies.citation: Preparing the World for Jesus (2nd ed., 2024), ch. 21 "The Misguided Greeks and Alexander's Ill-Fated Empire", PDF p. 567 (printed p. 553)

chronologies.date: “they lived but four hundred years before my time, as I believe”
chronologies.citation: Herodotus, Histories 2.53 (tr. George Rawlinson; Roman Roads Media etext, 2013), p. 119 (PDF p. 121)
chronologies.note: Homer and Hesiod: Herodotus's own opinion. DERIVED (not Herodotus's figure): 450 BC + 400 = about 850 BC. Anchor: CFAH-3 dates Herodotus's visit to Egypt to 450 B.C. (section "Conflicting Information: Herodotus Nine Centuries Below Moeris"; AP-21). About 50 years before Generations' "around 800 BC" for Homer (provisional); no tier 1–4 date.
